device.name: Wuji Hand left with soft pad (MuJoCo)

facts.text: The card's model is the MJCF robot model hand/body-with-soft/mjcf/left.xml, whose root element is <mujoco model="wujihand-left">
The model sets '<option jacobian="sparse" integrator="RK4" timestep="0.002" solver="Newton" iterations="50" tolerance="1e-10" />' and a default joint armature 0.0002 with damping 0.0
The model's worldbody root is the body left_palm_link
The root body left_palm_link declares an inertial and two mesh geoms and no joint before its first child body left_finger1_link1
The first finger joint left_finger1_joint1 declares no type attribute, axis 0 1 0, range 0.0475 1.6033, actuatorfrcrange -0.4452 0.4452 and armature 0.0005
The last finger joint left_finger5_joint4 declares range -0.4683 1.5735
The actuator section declares 20 position actuators, one per finger joint, each with kp, kv, ctrlrange and forcerange; the first, left_finger1_joint1_actuator, states ctrlrange 0.0475 1.6033
The last position actuator, left_finger5_joint4_actuator, states ctrlrange -0.4683 1.5735
The repository describes itself as a 'Robot model description package for the Wuji Hand and related accessories' providing URDF, MuJoCo (MJCF) and USD assets for simulation and visualization
The README describes hand/body-with-soft/ as the hand-body variant with a soft pad fixed to the thumb
The README's MuJoCo command loads a hand/body-with-soft model with 'python -m mujoco.viewer --mjcf=hand/body-with-soft/mjcf/right.xml'
The ROS2 package wuji_description is described as a robot model description package with URDF, MJCF and USD assets for simulation and ROS2 visualization
The CMake package installs the mjcf directory with the other model assets under share/wuji_description
display.launch.py returns three nodes, robot_state_publisher, joint_state_publisher_gui and rviz2, and no controller, command topic, service or action

determinism.notes: The stand-in integrates the same placeholder response for the same controls from the model defaults; it has no seed input and its motion is not MuJoCo's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the MJCF for the joint dimensions (20 hinges) and the 20 explicit actuator ctrlranges but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control target, so trajectories, contacts, soft-pad deformation, actuator kp/kv and forcerange dynamics and self-collision are not MuJoCo's
no STL mesh is loaded and no collision pair, equality, tendon or sensor of the model is resolved by the stand-in; the thumb soft-pad geometry is not simulated
the stand-in's snapshot and restore copy its placeholder arrays only; they say nothing about restoring a real MuJoCo state
the package serves only the card's first model, the left hand with soft pad; the right hand, the simplified collision variants, the hand/body model and the hand2 models are not served here
no rendering, camera or sensor stream is offered and no physical Wuji Hand is modelled or driven; nothing was validated against hardware
